question: Data set M has a mean of $58$ and a standard deviation of $9$. Data set N is formed by increasing each value in data set M by $12$. What is the standard deviation of data set N?

distractorNotes.B: reports the amount added to each value rather than the spread of the new data set.
distractorNotes.C: adds $12$ to the standard deviation, treating spread the same way as center.
distractorNotes.D: reports the mean of data set N instead of its standard deviation.

hint: Picture sliding every dot the same distance along the number line.
explanation:
**Choice A is correct.**

**The Fast Way (~30s):** Adding the same amount to every value slides the whole distribution without stretching it, so the standard deviation stays $9$.

**The Full Solution:**
Step 1: Each value of N is a value of M plus $12$, and the mean of N is $58 + 12 = 70$.
Step 2: Each deviation from the mean is unchanged, since $(x + 12) - (58 + 12) = x - 58$.
Step 3: Standard deviation is built entirely from those deviations, so it is still $9$. Check: the distances between values are unchanged by a shift, so the spread cannot change. $\checkmark$

**Why the wrong answers are tempting:**
* Choice B ($12$): reports the amount added to each value rather than the spread of the new data set.
* Choice C ($21$): adds $12$ to the standard deviation, treating spread the same way as center.
* Choice D ($70$): reports the mean of data set N instead of its standard deviation.

**Test Day Takeaway:** Adding a constant moves the center and leaves the spread alone. Only the mean and median shift by that constant.
